scope: Proposition 8.4 (Screening on retained walls) of the manuscript “Pure-Point Spectrum for the Two-Dimensional Anderson Model at Every Positive Disorder” (preprints/Pure-Point-Spectrum-for-the-Two-Dimensional-Anderson-Model-at-Every-Positive-Disorder-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 261 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 17487e3a2720b36f), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 51. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix an aligned square grid of side L∗, deterministic given the offset. Suppose a system retains the full stage-n data on a wall set containing strips of width δL∗ along every grid boundary, where δ > 0 is a fixed absolute constant. Count only good cores whose centers are at least 5Q1 inside this wall set, so that all their tests are intact. There is an absolute constant Aw such that, for L∗ sufficiently large at fixed n and AwL∗ ≤ r ≤ cbN , every crossing of the r-band has wall cost at least c′ nrα outside an event of conditional probability at most C′ nr−30. Here c′ n, C′ n and the threshold on L∗ may depend on n; Aw depends only on the absolute strip fraction and geometric constants. In particular, the constants in the bound are uniform as L∗ grows. As before, only edges within the crossed band need be counted.
